title: review: H4 fix round 4: the dispatch worker keeps a backward-compatible signature (executor or account id as an optional keyword) so test_fallback_claude_when_codex_cooling and other one-argument callers still work; full gate green (gate_red on T-0398)
spec:
STEP 0: the worktree must contain ade6b74, 530c2ab, c1ba47c, aca3bb2 and d54104f (T-0362, T-0392, T-0395, T-0398) in git log; never drop or amend them.
Gate red on T-0398 (daemon run; the Planner's external run confirms or adds to this): tests/test_executor.py::Executor::test_fallback_claude_when_codex_cooling fails with TypeError: the test's lambda takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given, then AssertionError Lists differ: [] != ['T-0007', 'T-0008']. Cause: d54104f (finding 1 of T-0397) passes the chosen executor or account id into the dispatch worker as a second positional argument, and the existing test replaces the worker with a one-argument lambda.
Fix: keep the worker call backward compatible: pass the chosen id as an optional keyword argument (default None means the worker selects as before), and make every call site and the spawn_async wrapper tolerate callers or mocks that accept one positional argument (try the keyword form, or pass it only when the callee accepts it via inspect.signature). Do not weaken test_fallback_claude_when_codex_cooling; if its mock must learn the new argument, extend the lambda to accept *args, **kwargs while keeping its assertions. Keep test_reservation_owner_matches_running_executor and the rest of the T-0362 lineage tests green. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh from the worktree root until it exits 0 (whole suite), then git add -A and git commit with the task id; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: git log --oneline in the worktree shows d54104f, aca3bb2, c1ba47c, 530c2ab and ade6b74 below your commit
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

comments.issue: executor.start()'s `finally: pool.release(task_id, ...)` fires unconditionally, including when the code returns via `_exhausted()`'s 'fallback' branch. That branch only *starts* a background thread (`run_worker(task_id, account_id=...)`) and returns immediately — the real work, and its own reserve/release cycle, happens asynchronously. So the reservation created by daemon.dispatch() (or by start() itself) for this task_id gets released the instant start() returns, before run_worker's thread has run its own `pool.reserve()`. This is not a rare corner case: it's the primary path whenever Codex is cooling (`fallback=True` in daemon.dispatch → account_id resolves to a Claude executor → `ex.provider != 'codex'` → `_exhausted` fallback). During the gap, the account's committed budget looks free, so a concurrent/subsequent dispatch decision (same tick loop or another thread) can reserve against the same headroom and over-commit past daily_budget/goal caps — the exact invariant test_parallel_reservations_cannot_exceed_daily_budget and the new budget-refusal tests are meant to protect, just not exercised end-to-end through this fallback path. Fix: only release in start()'s finally when the call actually owned/consumed the reservation synchronously (e.g. skip release when delegating to the async fallback thread, or pass reservation ownership into run_worker without releasing until it re-claims it).
